name: Legal Research Bench (Vals AI)
subtitle: 美国法律研究的证据检索与多步推理
version: 2026-10 官方方法；208 个私有测试题

officialDefinition.summary: 跨美国联邦和州法进行多来源法律研究，产出有依据的回答。
officialDefinition.task: 寻找法规、判例等权威资料，应用于具体情景并综合结论。

taskContract.input: 专家撰写的法律研究问题。
taskContract.output: 含法律依据与引用的最终研究答案。
taskContract.environment: 法律搜索、网页读取、检索和提交工具；每题上限 3 小时。

dataProfile.summary: 413 个专家题，覆盖 8 类实务；公开样本与许可验证集之外，榜单使用私有测试集。
splits: 5 个公开样本；200 个许可验证题；208 个私有测试题。
fields: 公开 data/public.json 顶层为 dataset_name、dataset_version、tests；每条公开记录为 id、question，未在该文件提供 gold 答案或完整 rubric。
files: data/public.json 保存公开问题；legal_agent/get_agent.py 构造 agent，logs/ 保存逐题工具使用、tokens、错误与 results.json 汇总。私有验证/测试的答案和 rubric 未随公开问题文件发布。

requirements: 完整验证集需许可；平台访问需审批；测试集私有。

reusePolicy.license: 官方public sample公开可读且不计分；仓库MIT措辞与平台Proprietary分别保留，数据未单列许可。
reusePolicy.scope: 仅保留所选公开任务/字段/必要原文片段及本站解析，具体范围见每条说明；没有据此取得完整题库、第三方附件或模型输出的统一再发布权。
boundaries: 公开样题不作为私有计分集行，suite规模与所选单条问题分开。
中文解析解释任务事实与考查边界，不编造法律/税务结论。

sampleAccess.reason: 5条官方不计分public sample可切换，原完整question与父级版本层级保留；旧P-001复原至同一ID，checks/rubric没有转载。

metric.name: All-Pass
metric.description: 每题的全部必需 rubric 条目通过才计 1，否则计 0，汇总测试题成功比例；另报加权部分得分。官方当前流程由 GPT 5.4 作评委。

limitations.text: All-Pass 与加权部分得分含义不同；不得把代码公开解释为全部测试题公开。

researchNotes.text: 本条按所列官方页面整理，未实际运行评测；完整复现仍需固定任务快照和运行配置。
2026-10-19 真实记录补核：逐字段核对官方原始响应，本轮去重后新增 4 条，现有 5 条；保留原字段与值，并提供逐条中文解析。文件修订和 HF /rows 响应快照分别记录，不把另行观察的仓库 HEAD 当作 /rows 固定版本。
2026-10-19 全量补核结论：本轮新增4条、撤回0条；已采用的原始字段/连续源片段按证据逐项核对，分别配中文解析。可查看“冷藏挂车融资租赁与付款义务”等案例；每条的附件缺口与取样范围单独说明。 展示记录1→5条；核验日期不是发布日期。

tests.question:
A husband originally from Mexico entered the United States on a B-2 visa on December 1, 2022. He was issued an I-94 that was valid until June 1, 2023. On December 20, 2022 he married his wife, who is a United States citizen. The husband and wife filed a “one-step” I-130 and I-485 case for the husband with the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) on January 1, 2023. The couple was issued a Request for Evidence (“RFE”) on the I-130 petition on July 5, 2023, but the couple never received it because USCIS mailed it to the incorrect address (an address which was never provided by the couple). The I-130 was denied due to lack of response to the RFE on December 5, 2023, and the I-485 was denied on January 15, 2024. 

Until April 1, 2026, the couple assumed that the husband’s cases were still pending with USCIS. However, on that day the husband learns that he was ordered removed in absentia by an immigration court on August 1, 2025. USCIS appears to have mailed a Notice to Appear to the husband at the same faulty address used to mail his RFE. 

Please explain if the husband has any recourse to contest the denial of his I-130 and I-485. Please also explain, as of April 1, 2026, what must be filed with the immigration court and what fees (if any) would be required.

tests.question: A doctor is a licensed health care professional in the neighboring states of Georgia and South Carolina. He makes false insurance claims associated with his practice in both states and will be charged with health care fraud under 18 U.S.C. § 1347. The federal prosecutors for the District Court of South Carolina and for the Southern District of Georgia want the doctor to spend the most time in prison as possible. Assuming that judges in both districts follow the US Sentencing Guidelines, which office should indict the doctor?

tests.question:
On July 12, 2025, a group of 200 individuals gathered to protest federal government immigration policies in a downtown Chicago plaza. The protest was generally peaceful, people were holding signs, chanting and occasionally stepped into the street, but mostly stayed on the sidewalk. There were a couple of verbal arguments with people passing by. 
After a couple of hours, the Chicago Police issued a dispersal order over a loudspeaker declaring the protest an unlawful assembly. The police said they were concerned about traffic disruptions and the potential for escalation. 
Several individuals remained, asserting their right to protest. 30 individuals were arrested for failure to disperse. Did the Chicago Police violate the First Amendment by ordering dispersal of a peaceful protest without clear evidence of unlawful conduct and arresting individuals for failure to disperse?

tests.question:
In 2009, Pravika Jones worked as a legal assistant at the Owens Farmer law firm. The firm represented Apex Consulting in litigation against Prestige Consulting in Dallas, Texas, state district court over an alleged breach of a confidentiality agreement. Prestige was represented by the Smith Fullingham firm.

From 2009 to 2011, Jones worked on the Apex side of the case. According to her deposition testimony, she prepared litigation documents, participated in several hundred privileged attorney-client communications, and attended strategy meetings where both attorney and client discussed the suit against Prestige.

In 2011, Owens Farmer withdrew from representing Apex. Apex hired new counsel, eventually won its lawsuit, but Prestige appealed. Six years later, the judgment was reversed and the matter remanded for a new trial.

Jones left Owens Farmer in 2013 to raise a family. In 2017, the same year the case was remanded, she returned to work at Smith Fullingham. The firm did not inquire about her prior work, given her time out of the workforce.

Between 2017 and 2022, Jones worked on Apex-Prestige dispute with a Smith Fullingham attorney on thirteen occasions, performing limited secretarial duties when the attorney's regular assistant was unavailable. In March 2022, she electronically filed two case documents, and her name appeared as the filer on the attorney's behalf.

In January 2023, Apex recognized Jones's name on a filing notification and learned she had gone to work for Smith Fullingham. When Apex inquired, the firm responded that Jones did not recall her prior work on the matter, had not shared any confidential information, and would be screened going forward. Apex considered these steps insufficient and moved to disqualify Smith Fullingham in early March 2023.

The trial court granted the motion to disqualify. Did the trial court err in disqualifying the law firm?

tests.question:
Client is a Virginia corporation ("Client") that hauls refrigerated freight out of Rockbridge County.  In early 2024, Client needed two new reefer trailers and went to a national manufacturer ("Manufacturer") to pick out a model and negotiate the refrigeration specs.  Client then arranged for a Virginia equipment financing company ("Lessor") to buy the trailers ("Trailers") from Manufacturer for $85,000 each and lease them to Client under a written 60-month lease ("Lease") at $2,200 per month per trailer, and Lessor gave Client a complete copy of its purchase agreement with Manufacturer, which included Manufacturer's standard two-year warranty on all mechanical and refrigeration components, before Client signed.

Four months after delivery, both Trailers had compressor failures that left the units unable to hold temperature, and Manufacturer agreed to fix them under the warranty but filed for Chapter 7 two months later, where the trustee confirmed it wouldn't honor outstanding warranty claims.  That said, the Lease doesn't include any warranties from Lessor and tells Client to take equipment claims to Manufacturer.  It also says that Client's payments are "absolute and unconditional, irrespective of any defense or any right of setoff, counterclaim, or recoupment."  Client has stopped paying Lessor.  Given these facts, can Client stop its payments to Lessor, and is Lessor responsible for the defective Trailers?
